name: table-fixed-date-erp-13-periods
description: ILLUSTRATIVE: a fixed_date year from 1 January with a table subdivision listing thirteen periods per year for 2023 to 2025, as an ERP period table import might: twelve periods of 28 days, then the rest of the year. The dates are invented. The table narrows the fixed_date rule to 2023-01-01 to 2025-12-31. The calendar is defined only between the table's first and last entry, so dates, year numbers, shifts, years, labels and dimension ranges outside it are OUT_OF_RANGE. A table subdivision does not split periods into weeks: weeks count from the fiscal year's first day, 'weeks' is null, the parent of a week is the year, and the weeks of a quarter or period are LEVEL_NOT_NESTED.

source.citation: Independent implementation of the spec in conformance/generators/fiscal_oracle.py, written with Python datetime and no fiscalclock code
source.checked_by: fiscal_oracle.py: Calendar.seq narrowed to the table's years; the table cross-block checks and naming_errors pass
